headline: Revenue dips as inventory charge and losses hit earnings
summary_short: Total revenue fell 2% year-over-year to $781.5 million as Tyvaso DPI growth was offset by a steep decline in Nebulized Tyvaso sales; net income dropped 15% to $274.9 million on a 44% rise in cost of sales and a swing to $46.3 million of net other expense.
summary_long: Revenue slipped 2% y/y to $781.5M: Tyvaso DPI grew 9% on higher volumes, but Nebulized Tyvaso fell 22% on lower U.S. volumes; Orenitram rose 12% while Remodulin fell 8%. Cost of sales jumped 44% y/y, driven by a higher inventory reserve including a $26.8M loss on a Tyvaso DPI supply agreement. R&D fell 7% on lower milestone payments; SG&A rose 8% on higher G&A and share-based comp. Other expense swung to a $46.3M net loss on unrealized equity-security losses, partly offset by a lower 14% effective tax rate (vs 24%). Net income fell 15% to $274.9M. No forward guidance was issued. Cash and equivalents fell to $1,279.7M; equity fell to $5,901.1M after a $1.5B accelerated share repurchase.

drivers.explanation: Tyvaso DPI volumes drove 9% growth, but Nebulized Tyvaso fell 22% on lower U.S. volumes, netting a 2% overall revenue decline.
Cost of sales rose 44% y/y mainly from a higher inventory reserve, including a $26.8 million estimated loss on a Tyvaso DPI supply agreement.
R&D expense fell 7% y/y, primarily from lower milestone payments for drug delivery device technology, partly offset by higher personnel costs.
SG&A rose 8% y/y on higher general and administrative costs and increased share-based compensation expense.
The effective tax rate fell to 14% from 24%, primarily due to increased excess tax benefits from share-based compensation.
Other expense swung to a $46.3 million net loss (from $4.3 million), mainly unrealized losses on equity securities, driving most of the 15% net income decline.
Equity fell as the board authorized a $2.0 billion buyback in March 2026, with $1.5 billion executed via an accelerated share repurchase with Citibank.
Management said the competitive landscape for inhaled prostacyclins remains dynamic and is targeting a return to sequential quarterly revenue growth.
